statements.new_statement_en: Soldiers, reservists, veterans and bereaved military families should receive more payments and benefits from the state, even if this requires raising taxes.

reason: The weighty bills are one issue: more state benefits for people who serve or served (reservist student aid, daycare, property-tax discounts, tax credits, unemployment and maternity pay, disabled-veteran and discharged-soldier rights, conscript combat pay, priority in land and civil-service hiring), with row 9 (removing benefits from senior defense officials) pointing the other way. The current text fits the core but leaves out a large weighty block: bereaved families of fallen soldiers (rows 3, 11, 13, 16, 22, 30) and serving conscripts (rows 21, 32, 35). A minimal rewrite names these groups; it keeps one demand (more benefits), the price (raising taxes) and the agree key '+'. Row 26 (hospital security work counted as preferred work) is off-topic but light.
